Definition: violent; by implication deadly; also (in a good sense) brave
BiblicalUsage: Four times, and the word never softens. The wine of false gods is the cruel venom of asps; Job says God has become cruel to me; of Leviathan, none is so fierce that dare stir him up; and Lamentations says the daughter of God's people is become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness. Cruelty is laid at the door of idols, of Leviathan, of a ruined city — and once, in his agony, at the door of God.
TheologicalSignificance: Job's charge is the one that stops me. He says it to God's face, in his suffering, and God does not strike him for it — He answers him. I hold that this is the Bible's honesty about pain: the sufferer may say the hard thing, and God is big enough to hear it and answer.
